name: Soyboy Vs Yes Chad
core: A crying, ranting wojak objects to something while the calm Nordic gamer Chad simply accepts it.
avoid: Not for balanced, nuanced comparisons.

name: Car Salesman Slaps Roof Of Car
core: A salesman slaps the roof of a car and boasts how much 'this bad boy' can fit or do.
avoid: Not for honest product reviews.

name: Chill Guy
core: A relaxed dog-like guy in a sweater stays totally unbothered, used to describe staying chill despite chaos.
aliases: my new character is a chill guy
avoid: Not for panic or anger.

name: Jackie Chan WTF
core: Jackie Chan clutches his head in total bafflement at something that makes no sense.
avoid: Not for things that make perfect sense.

name: The Office Congratulations
core: A boss shakes young Michael Scott's hand in congratulations, used for being rewarded for something dubious or minor.
avoid: Not for genuine heartfelt achievements.

name: And Just Like That
core: Forrest Gump gazes off as something suddenly changes or ends, captioned 'and just like that...'.
avoid: Not for slow, gradual changes.

name: Happy Star Congratulations
core: A cheesy kids' award certificate sarcastically congratulating someone for a tiny or dumb achievement.
avoid: Not for sincere big accomplishments.

name: Keep Calm And Carry On
core: A parody of the British wartime poster, swapping in new advice in the 'Keep Calm and ...' format.
avoid: Not for panicked or chaotic messages.

name: Megamind No Bitches
core: Megamind leans in with a smug stare asking 'No ___?' to mock someone for lacking something.
avoid: Not for sincere questions.

name: The Future World If
core: A utopian futuristic city showing how amazing the world would be if some small thing happened.
avoid: Not for things that would make the world worse.

name: Obama Medal
core: Obama awards a medal to himself, used when someone congratulates themselves or a thing praises itself.
avoid: Not for praise that genuinely comes from someone else.

name: Arthur Fist
core: A clenched fist showing suppressed rage or frustration at something annoying that you can't openly react to.
avoid: Not for genuine anger or violence; it's for petty, bottled-up irritation.

name: Peter Griffin News
core: Peter Griffin's 'What Really Grinds My Gears' segment, used to rant about a petty pet peeve.
avoid: Not for serious grievances or praise; it's for petty complaints.

name: Bell Curve (IQ)
core: The dumb take and the genius take agree; only the overthinking midwit in the middle disagrees.
avoid: Jokes where the middle opinion is right.

name: Inception
core: Characters proposing to go a level deeper, used for nested or recursive ideas that spiral absurdly.
avoid: Not for simple one-step comparisons; it needs a nested or recursive idea.

name: Kermit Window
core: Kermit gazing sadly out a rainy window, used for melancholy, longing or quietly waiting for something that won't come.
avoid: Not for happy or energetic moments.

name: Spongegar
core: Primitive caveman SpongeBob, used to mock primitive, simplistic or outdated thinking and behavior.
avoid: Not for sophisticated or clever ideas.

name: Liam Neeson Taken
core: Liam Neeson's Taken phone call: 'I will find you', used as an over-the-top threat about a minor offense.
avoid: Not for real threats or serious crimes.

name: Peter Parker Cry
core: J. Jonah Jameson dismisses Peter's hopeful answer and laughs, leaving Peter in tears; used for having your hopes crushed.
avoid: Not for happy outcomes; the hope must get crushed.

name: Well Yes, But Actually No
core: A pirate captain's 'Well yes, but actually no', used to contradict a question or claim that seems true but isn't.
avoid: Not for clear agreement; the answer has to be a twisty no.

name: Gollum
core: Gollum's creepy eager grin, used for obsessive greed over something you treasure ('my precious').
avoid: Not for calm or wholesome moments.

name: Moe Throws Barney
core: Moe throws Barney out of the bar, but Barney is back inside moments later; used for something you got rid of that instantly returns.
avoid: Not for permanent fixes; the thing has to return.

name: Kevin Hart Stare
core: Kevin Hart's wide-eyed suspicious stare, used when someone says something shocking, sketchy or unbelievable.
avoid: Not for happy approval; it's for disbelief.

name: Grim Reaper Knocking Door
core: Death knocks on door after door, each victim behind one; used when a threat has taken out others and is now coming for you or the next one.
avoid: Not for real deaths or tragedies.

name: Undertaker Behind
core: The Undertaker appears menacingly behind a celebrating wrestler; used when someone is enjoying a moment, unaware of the doom about to arrive.
avoid: Not for pleasant surprises.

name: Satisfied Seal
core: A smug, contented seal, used for small petty victories or quiet satisfaction.
avoid: Not for frustration or bad news.

name: Leonardo DiCaprio Wolf Of Wall Street Laughing
core: Leo grins, then bursts out laughing; used when something is funny and then gets even funnier, or for laughing at someone's naivety.
slots: the punchline that makes it funnier
avoid: Not for sad or serious moments.

name: Spiderman Computer Desk
core: Spider-Man sits at a desk under a portrait of himself, used for smug or absurd self-referential statements and dry deadpan announcements.
avoid: Not for emotional reactions; it's deadpan.

name: Presidential Alert
core: A phone's emergency Presidential Alert, used to announce something trivial as if it were a national emergency.
avoid: Not for real emergencies or disasters.

name: Google Did You Mean
core: A Google search where Google 'corrects' your query to something funnier or more honest; used to reveal what you really meant.
avoid: Not for photo reactions; it's a text-swap joke.

name: Giga Chad
core: The idealized, impossibly confident Giga Chad, used to portray someone or something as the ultimate effortless alpha choice.
avoid: Not for weakness or failure.

name: Who Wants To Be A Millionaire
core: A shocked contestant faces a quiz question with four answers, used for trick questions where every option is bad or the answer is obvious.
aliases: who wants to be a millionaire
avoid: Not for single-statement reactions; it needs a question and options.

name: It's Not Going To Happen
core: Regina George from Mean Girls telling someone to stop trying to make something happen, because it's not going to happen.
slots: stop trying to make X happen
aliases: stop trying to make fetch happen
avoid: Not for encouragement or things that are catching on.

name: Hold Fart
core: A student straining with a tense face, used for desperately holding something in or trying hard not to react.
avoid: Not for relaxed or calm moments.

name: Y'all Got Any More Of That
core: Tyrone Biggums twitchily begging for more of something, used when someone is hooked on a thing and craves more of it.
slots: y'all got any more of that X
aliases: y'all got any more of that
avoid: Not for things nobody would crave; it's about addictive wanting.

name: Lisa Simpson's Presentation
core: Lisa presents a statement on a screen as if it were an undeniable fact, used for blunt truths or hot takes stated with authority.
avoid: Not for multi-step stories or dialogue; one statement only.

name: I'm Something Of A Scientist Myself
core: Norman Osborn smugly claims expertise, used when someone with minimal skill compares themselves to experts.
slots: I'm something of a X myself
avoid: Not for real experts; the joke is unearned confidence.

name: Peter Parker Smirk
core: Peter Parker's sly sideways smirk, used for feeling smug or quietly mischievous about something.
avoid: Not for genuine sadness or anger.

name: Sure Grandma Let's Get You To Bed
core: A young woman gently escorts a rambling grandma away, used to dismiss an outdated or absurd claim condescendingly.
slots: sure grandma, let's get you to bed
avoid: Not for mocking real elderly people; it's about dismissing silly takes.

name: Smiling Cat
core: A wide-eyed cat with an awkward forced smile, used for nervously pretending everything is fine or innocently hiding something.
avoid: Not for genuine joy or anger.

name: Obi Wan Kenobi
core: Old Obi-Wan delivering wise-sounding but evasive lines, used for technically-true excuses or nostalgic remarks.
aliases: from a certain point of view
avoid: Not for direct, angry reactions.

name: That's A Paddlin'
core: Jasper holding a paddle declares any petty offense punishable, used to mock strict rules or warn against a small annoying behaviour.
avoid: Not for serious real-world punishment.

name: Jason Momoa Henry Cavill
core: Jason Momoa creeps up grinning behind an unaware Henry Cavill, used for a problem or person sneaking up on someone oblivious.
avoid: Not for open confrontations; the target must be oblivious.

name: Floating Boy Chasing Running Boy
core: A boy floats eerily down a hallway after a fleeing boy, used for something inescapable pursuing someone.
avoid: Not for things you can easily escape.

name: Blank Starter Pack
core: A titled grid of items that stereotypically come with a type of person or situation, used to roast a familiar archetype.
avoid: Not for a single punchline; needs several telling items.

name: Bender
core: Bender in a fur coat smugly declaring he'll do his own thing, used for spitefully making your own version of something that excluded you.
slots: I'll make my own, with X
avoid: Not for humble or sincere moments.

name: Confused Mr Krabs
core: Mr Krabs spinning in a blur of confusion, used when overwhelmed or utterly lost in a situation.
avoid: Not for calm understanding or confidence.

name: Here's Johnny
core: Jack Torrance leering through a broken door, used for something unwelcome forcing its way back in or a menacing arrival.
avoid: Not for pleasant or welcome arrivals.

name: Yes Honey
core: A smiling woman makes a request and a weary wojak man submits, used for tired, automatic agreement with a demand.
avoid: Not for enthusiastic agreement.

name: Wolverine Remember
core: Wolverine wistfully gazing at a framed picture, used for nostalgically missing something from the past.
slots: the thing I miss in the frame
avoid: Not for things you're glad are gone.

name: Rick And Carl
core: Rick sets up a dad joke and delivers the pun while Carl stares down in annoyance, used for groan-worthy puns.
avoid: Not for serious conversations; needs a pun.

name: Angry Baby
core: A baby screaming in outrage, used for overreacting with fury to a small inconvenience.
avoid: Not for calm or happy moments.

name: Milk Carton
core: A missing-person milk carton, used to joke that something has gone missing or disappeared for ages.
avoid: Not for real missing people.

name: The Office Handshake
core: An awkward, forced handshake between two parties, used when two unlikely sides make an uneasy deal or agreement.
avoid: Not for genuine, warm partnerships.

name: Pentagon Hexagon Octagon
core: Three real shapes followed by an absurd '-agon' pun in the empty fourth panel, used for wordplay on any word ending in 'gone'.
avoid: Not for captions that aren't an '-agon' pun.

name: I Am Once Again Asking
core: Bernie Sanders' weary repeated plea, used to ask for the same thing yet again.
aliases: i am once again asking for your financial support
avoid: Not for first-time or one-off requests.

name: Chef Gordon Ramsay
core: Gordon Ramsay screaming in the kitchen, used for furious, brutally honest criticism of poor work.
avoid: Not for gentle or constructive feedback.

name: Guess I'll Die
core: An old man shrugging in resignation, used when there's no way out of a bad situation and you just accept doom.
avoid: Not for situations with an easy fix.

name: I Fear No Man
core: The TF2 Heavy says he fears no man, but that thing scares him; the blank panel shows the one harmless-looking thing that terrifies you.
aliases: but that thing it scares me
avoid: Not for things that are genuinely, obviously dangerous.

name: Achievement Unlocked
core: An Xbox achievement badge, used to sarcastically celebrate a tiny, dubious or embarrassing accomplishment.
avoid: Not for genuinely big milestones meant seriously.
